description: Influencer management actions and customer self-service. Covers the remaining Phase 6 checklist items: manage services and availability + block dates; manual actions (resend link, cancel, reschedule); and a customer self-service page reached by a signed link to reschedule or cancel. Reuses the dashboard access + Message/email + shared-event logic from FEAT-002 and FEAT-003. Signed links use lib/signing.ts exactly as the Google connect flow does. Reschedule/cancel must update the Google Calendar event and re-notify, consistent with the overview status machine (CANCELLED side-exit) and the existing meeting/alerts patterns. Depends on FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: Block dates: add the data model for blocked dates. Add a BlockedDate model (or availability exception) to prisma/schema.prisma keyed by influencerId with a date (and optional reason), @map snake_case, indexed by influencerId. Add a matching hand-written SQL migration (timestamp after FEAT-003's). Then make slot generation respect it: in lib/slots.ts (generateSlots / isSlotStart) or at the query layer in app/api/slots/route.ts and the hold validation in app/api/bookings/hold/route.ts, exclude any slot whose day is blocked for that influencer, so customers cannot book blocked dates. Keep the pure slot math testable.

Manage services + availability (influencer-authenticated via the signed dashboard token): add API routes under app/api/dashboard/ (or app/api/manage/) to create/update/deactivate services (title, description, durationMin, priceMinor, currency, type, capacity, active) and to create/update/delete availability_rules and blocked dates. Validate bodies with zod and map named errors to HTTP status exactly like app/api/checkout/route.ts and app/api/bookings/hold/route.ts. Every mutating route must verify the signed dashboard token (same purpose string as FEAT-003) and that the targeted service/rule belongs to that influencer; reject otherwise with 403/404.

Add the management UI to the dashboard client component (built on FEAT-003's seams): forms to add/edit services, edit weekly availability rules, and block/unblock dates, using the existing CSS classes. Keep it minimal and consistent with BookingFlow.tsx.

Manual actions per booking: implement resend-link, cancel, and reschedule as signed-token-gated API routes. RESEND: re-send the confirmation (enqueueSendMessage / sendBookingEmail) and record a Message row; do not create a new event. CANCEL: set booking status CANCELLED, cancel/remove the attendee from the Calendar event (for a 1:1 delete the event; for a GROUP remove just that attendee from the shared event and only delete the event when the last attendee leaves), re-notify, and flag the payment needsRefund if it was CAPTURED (follow lib/payment-webhook.ts needsRefund usage). RESCHEDULE: move the Session (or move the booking to another session) and update the Calendar event start/end via a new lib/google.ts updateEvent method (events.patch with new start/end, sendUpdates=all), then re-notify. All of this must keep lib/meeting.ts idempotency and the shared-group-event invariant intact.

Extend lib/google.ts with the update/delete event capability needed above (e.g. patchEvent for new times, and removing an attendee / deleting the event), reusing classifyCalendarError and the existing fetch/call wrapper. Extend lib/meeting.ts (or a new lib/manage.ts) with the domain functions cancelBooking / rescheduleBooking / resendBookingLink that orchestrate DB update + calendar update + notification + Message recording, each wrapped so a calendar/alert failure is handled like the existing create path (named errors, best-effort alerts).

Customer self-service: add a signed-link helper in lib/signing.ts usage (new purpose string, e.g. 'customer-self-service') and generate the link when the booking is confirmed (include it in the confirmation email/message from FEAT-003). Add a public page under app/booking/[token]/ (or app/manage/[token]/) that verifies the token, shows the customer their booking, and offers Reschedule (pick a new available slot via the existing /api/slots) and Cancel. Add the customer-facing API routes that verify the self-service token (NOT the dashboard token) and call the same rescheduleBooking / cancelBooking domain functions. Invalid/expired token -> friendly 403 page, mirroring app/api/google/callback/route.ts static-message style.

Tests: add pure unit tests where possible, e.g. tests/blocked-dates.test.ts asserting that a blocked day removes its slots from generateSlots (DB-free, like tests/slots.test.ts), and a test for the self-service token round-trip using lib/signing.ts signToken/verifyToken (like tests/signature.test.ts: valid token verifies, tampered/expired/wrong-purpose token rejects). Keep calendar/DB-dependent paths out of the pure tests; note any that need CI.

Update doc/06-groups-and-dashboard.md to check off the remaining tasks (manage services/availability/block dates, manual actions, customer self-service). Confirm the 'Done when' criterion is satisfied in the write-up: five customers can book one group session, all get the same link, and the influencer sees them in the dashboard. Update README.md with a brief Phase 6 section (dashboard link script, self-service link) in the style of the existing Phase 3 section.
acceptance_criteria: A BlockedDate (or availability-exception) model exists with a matching migration, and blocked days are excluded from both /api/slots results and hold validation so they cannot be booked

Signed-token-gated management routes can create/update/deactivate services and create/update/delete availability rules and blocked dates, with zod validation and ownership checks (403/404 on mismatch), matching existing route conventions

Manual actions work end to end in code: resend re-sends + records a Message; cancel sets CANCELLED, updates the Calendar event (removes attendee from a shared group event / deletes a 1:1 event), re-notifies, and flags needsRefund for captured payments; reschedule moves the session and patches the Calendar event times and re-notifies
lib/google.ts gained event update/delete/remove-attendee methods reusing the existing error classification

A customer self-service page reached by a signed link lets a customer reschedule or cancel their own booking, gated by a self-service token distinct from the dashboard token, with an invalid/expired token showing a friendly 403
Pure unit tests cover blocked-date slot exclusion and the self-service signed-token round-trip without a live DB
verification: Static validation: grep that every new route verifies a signed token before mutating, that self-service routes use the customer purpose string and management routes use the dashboard purpose string (not interchangeable), and that every Prisma field/enum referenced (BlockedDate.*, Booking.status CANCELLED, Payment.needsRefund) matches prisma/schema.prisma
Confirm new migration table/column names match the Prisma @map names and the migration timestamp is after FEAT-003's
Read cancelBooking/rescheduleBooking and confirm a GROUP cancel removes only the one attendee from the shared event (and deletes only when empty), preserving the shared-event invariant from FEAT-002
Read tests/blocked-dates.test.ts and the self-service token test and confirm they would fail if blocked dates were ignored or if an expired/wrong-purpose token were accepted
In a normal environment: `npx prisma generate`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (CI-only here; note in findings)

findings.summary: Implemented the remaining Phase 6 items: block dates, influencer management (services/availability/blocked dates + per-booking resend/cancel/reschedule), lib/google event update/delete/remove-attendee, lib/manage.ts domain functions, and customer self-service via a distinct signed link. All validated statically (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY: no npm/prisma/tsc/next/tsx), plus the two new pure test suites' logic verified in plain node.
findings.blocked_dates: prisma/schema.prisma gained a BlockedDate model (id, influencerId @map("influencer_id") FK onDelete Cascade, date DateTime @db.Date, reason?, createdAt @map("created_at"), @@unique([influencerId, date]), @@index([influencerId]), @@map("blocked_dates")) plus an Influencer.blockedDates relation. Hand-written migration prisma/migrations/20261012000000_blocked_dates/migration.sql (timestamp later than FEAT-003's 20261011000000; provider unchanged) CREATE TABLE blocked_dates + the unique+index + FK, mirroring the 20261009000000 style; verified column/index/constraint names match the @map names. lib/slots.ts: generateSlots and isSlotStart gained an optional blockedDates: ReadonlySet<string> (YYYY-MM-DD) that drops any rule day whose date is in the set, keeping the math pure; added blockedDaySet(dates) that reads the stored UTC-midnight day back to YYYY-MM-DD. Both /api/slots and /api/bookings/hold load the influencer's blocked days (a +/-1 day window) and pass them in, so a blocked day yields no slots AND cannot be held.
findings.google_client: lib/google.ts GoogleClient gained updateEvent (events.patch new start/end, conferenceDataVersion=1&sendUpdates=all; 404/410 -> GoogleRequestError), removeAttendee (GET event, drop the matching email, PATCH sendUpdates=all; returns {remaining} so the caller deletes once empty; idempotent and 404/410 -> remaining 0), and deleteEvent (DELETE sendUpdates=all; 404/410 treated as already-deleted/idempotent). All reuse classifyCalendarError and the existing call() wrapper. insertEvent/getEvent/addAttendee unchanged.
findings.domain_functions: New lib/manage.ts with named errors (ManageBlockedError = needs reconnect, DB kept; ManageRejectedError = Google rejected for good; BookingNotManageableError) and injectable ManageDeps. resendBookingLink: records a queued whatsapp Message + sendBookingEmail + enqueueSendMessage, no event change. cancelBooking: sets CANCELLED, flags any CAPTURED Payment needsRefund (mirrors lib/payment-webhook.ts), then best-effort calendar: 1:1 -> deleteEvent(booking.eventId); GROUP -> removeAttendee from the session-derived shared event and deleteEvent + clear session.eventId/meetLink only when remaining===0 (preserves the FEAT-002 shared-event invariant), then re-notifies. rescheduleBooking: guards future-time + slot clash, moves the Session start/end, patches the event (session event for GROUP, booking event for 1:1) via updateEvent, re-notifies every live booking in the session. Calendar failures are best-effort (lastError recorded + alertInfluencer), rethrown as ManageBlockedError/ManageRejectedError; transient failures swallowed after the DB change (influencer alerted, retryable from dashboard).
findings.signed_links_and_routes: lib/self-service.ts holds SELF_SERVICE_PURPOSE ('customer-self-service', DISTINCT from DASHBOARD_LINK_PURPOSE and CONNECT_LINK_PURPOSE), buildSelfServiceUrl(bookingId) -> /manage/<token>, verifySelfServiceToken; kept in its own module (no DB/email imports) so lib/email.ts embeds the link in the confirmation/receipt without an import cycle through lib/manage.ts (manage re-exports them for convenience). lib/dashboard.ts gained verifyDashboardToken. Management routes under app/api/dashboard/ (services POST/PATCH, availability POST/PATCH/DELETE, blocked-dates POST/DELETE, bookings/[id] POST resend|cancel|reschedule) each verifyDashboardToken FIRST (403) and check the target belongs to the influencer (404), zod-validate bodies, and map named errors to status like app/api/checkout. Customer route app/api/manage/[token] verifies the SELF-SERVICE token (never the dashboard token; the token itself carries the booking id so there is no spoofable ownership lookup) and calls the same cancel/reschedule functions. A reconnect-needed calendar failure returns 202 with a warning (DB change already applied).
findings.ui: app/manage/[token]/page.tsx (server) verifies the self-service token before loading anything -> friendly 403 on invalid/expired (404 if booking gone), in the static-message spirit of app/api/google/callback. app/manage/[token]/ManageBooking.tsx (client) shows the booking and offers Reschedule (new slot via /api/slots) + Cancel. app/dashboard/page.tsx now also loads services/rules/blockedDates and passes them to app/dashboard/Dashboard.tsx, which gained management forms (add/deactivate service, add/delete weekly rule, block/unblock day) and per-booking Resend/Cancel/Reschedule buttons, all reusing existing globals.css classes (card/muted/error/slots/slot/primary/choice/check). The read-only seams (token + booking ids) from FEAT-003 were reused unchanged.
findings.tests: tests/blocked-dates.test.ts (pure, like tests/slots.test.ts): a blocked day removes all its slots from generateSlots; blocking one day leaves other days; isSlotStart rejects a real start on a blocked day; blockedDaySet maps a stored UTC-midnight date to YYYY-MM-DD. tests/self-service.test.ts (pure, like tests/signature.test.ts, uses an explicit key so no APP_SECRET/DB): valid token round-trips to the booking id; tampered body, expired, wrong-purpose (dashboard purpose) and wrong-key tokens are all rejected. The signing round-trip + rejection assertions and the blockedDaySet mapping were re-run in plain node (env -u NODE_OPTIONS) and pass; the generateSlots assertions depend on luxon so they run in CI.
findings.validation_ci_only: Per the FEAT-001 sandbox constraint, these could NOT run here and are CI-only: npx prisma generate, npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit), next build, and npm test via tsx (needs node_modules + @/* alias; luxon is a placeholder here). Static validation performed: read every new/changed file for TS correctness; grep-confirmed updateEvent/removeAttendee/deleteEvent exported from lib/google.ts and used in lib/manage.ts; verifyDashboardToken used by all management routes and verifySelfServiceToken by all self-service routes/page (purposes not interchangeable); confirmed every Prisma field/enum referenced (BlockedDate.* and its @map names, Booking.status CANCELLED, Payment.status CAPTURED + needsRefund + failureReason, Session.eventId/meetLink) matches prisma/schema.prisma and that the new migration names match the model; verified generateSlots/isSlotStart's new param is optional so existing callers are unaffected.
findings.deviations: Reschedule moves the booking's Session (not a move to a different session). For a GROUP that means the whole shared session moves to the new time, which keeps the one-event-per-session invariant intact and is the sensible semantics (you cannot move a single attendee out of a shared Meet event onto a new time without breaking the group). The customer self-service token TTL defaults to 30 days (vs 7 for the dashboard link) since it travels in the confirmation email and must outlive it. The dashboard Reschedule button uses a prompt() for the ISO time to stay minimal; the customer self-service page uses the full /api/slots picker. A reconnect-needed calendar failure returns HTTP 202 (DB change applied, calendar pending) rather than an error, so the influencer/customer is not told the whole action failed.
findings.review_fixes_2026_10_08: Addressed the 2026-10-08-140007 review. (2/3) rescheduleBooking now validates newStart before moving the session: a new pure validateRescheduleTime(rules,durationMin,newStart,blockedDates,now) mirrors the hold route (future + isSlotStart against availability rules + blocked days loaded around the target); it throws the new RescheduleNotAllowedError (mapped to 409 in both app/api/dashboard/bookings/[id] and app/api/manage/[token]). The session move now runs inside prisma.$transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the session row (mirroring lib/holds.ts) plus the existing clash check, re-counting activeSeatWhere seats against service.capacity so a shrunk capacity cannot let a reschedule oversell. loadBooking now includes influencer.rules for the validation. (4) app/api/dashboard/services PATCH now rejects (409) lowering capacity below the max active seats on any live session and rejects changing service type while sessions with live bookings exist (uses a filtered _count of activeSeatWhere bookings per session). (7) Dashboard message status switched from a single latest row to the latest row PER CHANNEL: app/dashboard/page.tsx loads the last 20 messages and reduces to one-per-channel (latestPerChannel), Dashboard.tsx BookingView.latestMessage became messages: MessageView[] and messagesLabel joins them, so a later queued whatsapp row no longer hides an earlier failed email. (5) Group reschedule re-notifying every attendee (one confirmation email per booking) is confirmed intended and documented in a code comment and doc/06. New DB-free tests in tests/manage.test.ts: four validateRescheduleTime cases (past / off-rules / blocked-day / accepted) and two mock.module-based group-cancel cases (removes only the leaving attendee when others remain; deletes the shared event and clears session.eventId/meetLink when the last leaves). All static-only here (INTEGRATIONS_ONLY): grep-verified RescheduleNotAllowedError exported+mapped in both routes, activeSeatWhere imported in services route and manage.ts, _count filtered-relation syntax is Prisma 7 GA, and all referenced Prisma fields match schema.
